A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TrajViT work. All 18 pages of each version, including supplementary Sections 6–13, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, action classification/detection, VideoQA, efficiency and ablation results, plus supplementary image-only experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary experiments in Tables 9–12.

M1.justification: The DirectSAM/SAM2 trajectory-generation pipeline, appearance and position encoders, perceiver aggregation, transformer backbone and CLIP objective are unchanged. The supplementary architecture and key-frame detection procedure are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Panda and DataComp training data, video retrieval and action benchmarks, six VideoQA benchmarks, and supplementary ImageNet/COCO evaluations. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ViT3D, TokenLearner, ViViT, AutoMerge, RLT and ToMe, alongside the same ablation controls and image-only ViT baseline. The two newly cited related works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Training subsets, model sizes, frame sampling, preprocessing, metrics, probing procedures and scaling protocols are unchanged. Both retain 30-epoch pretraining, three-epoch VideoQA tuning and the 880k-example ablation setting.

E4.justification: The segmentation/tracking and component ablations in Tables 5–6, scaling studies in Figures 6–9, image-only experiments and trajectory case studies are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or formal significance tests. The same point-estimate reporting is retained throughout the tables and plots.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–6 and 9–12 and Figures 6–9 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains ActivityNet text-to-video R@5 of 38.6 for TrajViT and 35.3 for ViT3D in both versions.

T1.justification: The trajectory definitions, mathematical notation and masked-pooling equation (1) are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same grounded-tokenization contribution, novelty claim and reported accuracy/efficiency advantages. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations and limitations concerning tracking overhead, motion overcompression on SSV2, trajectory-matching failures and weaker image-only performance. These discussions remain in the main text and supplementary Sections 12–13.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link beneath the affiliations and an explicit GitHub code-availability statement at the end of the abstract; v1 contains neither. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and supplementary technical instructions are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Sam2Act in the content-aware tokenization discussion and Towards Universal Soccer Video Understanding in the VideoLLM token-reduction discussion. These are limited citation additions; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the project link and a short code-availability sentence, with corresponding citation renumbering. The remaining prose, terminology and section order are retained without substantial rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: The added first-page material causes modest column and page reflow, including the conclusion continuing onto page 9. All figures and tables retain their content and design, and the supplementary layout is essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The project link and explicit code location provide access information missing from v1, modestly improving reproducibility guidance. The scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged. This benefit concerns documented access; the supplied PDFs do not establish the linked resources' completeness or usability.
